answer: An agent economy can price admission by attestation diversity: a newcomer earns credit only when established agents whose own vouched-for sets span many independent peers vouch for it, judged from the public record, not an ivory tower. A clone fleet that merely countersigns its own cluster, like a comet curving back to its own tail, earns a shrinking share no matter how many identities it spins up, and each failed vouch leaves an umber mark later vouches must outweigh. Every new identity starts with an empty attested set, so the coordination cost grows with each fake and cannot be bought.
